newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Sun Alliance sees positive NZ medium-term growth.
newsitem.headline: Sun Alliance sees positive NZ medium-term growth.

text.p: Fund manager Sun Alliance said it saw positive medium-term growth in New Zealand under the policies of the new centre-right coalition government but the direction of the New Zealand dollar remained "the big unknown".
Sun Alliance said in its 1996 annual report that somewhat looser monetary policy and higher government spending by the coalition were favourable for overall investment activity.
It expected higher activity in some sectors such as construction, where more funds would be spent on roading, hospitals and schools.

Although exporters and politicians were trying to talk the New Zealand dollar down, Sun Allance said the currency had not budged and relatively high short-term rates would still attract offshore investors to New Zealand.
"For this reason, don't be surprised if the currency does not fall as much as the pundits are hoping it will," Investment Manager Bill Courtney said.
He said the strong Kiwi dollar eroded some market returns from Sun Alliance's international funds. The global fund, for example, returned only 1.2 percent after tax.
"We have recently changed our long-term policy on currency hedging and are now prepared to hedge at least part of the currency exposure, if we believe it is appropriate," Sun Alliance said.
It said the global outlook was dominated by prospects for the U.S. stockmarket.
"We are still uneasy about the high valuation of this market and are therefore cautious about the short-term outlook. Other major markets, particularly in Europe, offer better value."

New Zealand assets had been the main drivers of the Conservative and Balanced Funds as they reacted favourably to the outcome of last October's election. The funds returned 5.5 percent and 5.0 percent respectively, tax-paid.

The New Zealand Shares fund achieved a 15.5 percent tax-paid return over its first full six months, while the new Smaller Companies fund returned 28.0 percent over six months. The main contributors to the latter were Lyttelton Port, which makes up 6.6 percent of the fund, Fletcher Building (11.5 percent), and Ports of Auckland (9.5 percent).
The European fund returned 11.2 percent after tax over the year but the Far East and Emerging Markets funds disappointed, with returns of minus 4.6 percent and minus 2.9 percent respectively.
Sun Alliance is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Royal and Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc. Funds under management in New Zealand exceeded NZ$850 million in 1996.
